correctness.rationale: PASS: hyperbolic polar-volume CDF yields R-r_i=>independent Exp(d-1) in common-quantile coupling; Y_i=e^{R-r_i} are Pareto(d-1). Hyperbolic cosine law gives b_ij=r_i+r_j+2log sin(theta_ij/2)+o(1), half-angle identity yields alpha_i~2e^-r_i s_jk/(s_ij s_ik), and Gauss–Bonnet converts into W_d. Conditional finite Pareto convolution tail is sum a_i^(d-1) by one-big-jump argument. For p<d-1, triangle inequality a_i≤2(1/s_ij+1/s_ik) and Haar small-angle probability O(delta^(d-1)) imply integrability; p≥d-1 diverges from independent Y_i. Numerically recomputed equiangular d=2 example e^R*(pi-A_R) at R=5,7,9: 6.927749,6.928195,6.928203 vs 4sqrt3=6.928203. Claims only limit-variable moments, not finite-R moment convergence.
